messages:
Eve Tran: Heads upwe need a concise canary gate for onboarding models that includes quant experiments. Current canary runs are inconsistent and block automation.

Diego Morales: Agreed. Proposal: a "canary-40" small suite (40 curated prompts) that covers top 10 intents + 10 adversarial/template variants. Keep latency-friendly and deterministic seeds.

Hannah Li: Metrics to export: schema_accuracy (field-level correctness for structured responses), normalized_levenshtein (for small formatting diffs), embed_cosine_mean (semantic drift), and token_coverage (fraction of tokens produced vs baseline to catch truncation).

Marta Ruiz: Threshold ideas: schema_accuracy >= 0.92, norm_levenshtein <= 0.06, embed_cosine_mean >= 0.82, token_coverage >= 0.98. Also require no intent to regress > 3pp absolute.

Eve Tran: Include a stats rule: bootstrap 2000 samples, alpha=0.04. Use Benjamini-Hochberg for multiple metrics. Treat a metric as regressed only if p < alpha after correction and relative drop > 1.8%.

Diego Morales: Add action flags in the policy JSON so CI can choose: HOLD_CANARY (auto-block + open ticket), WARN_ONLY (notify owners), or INCONCLUSIVE (run full regression). Put a link to the run artifacts in the ticket.

Hannah Li: Small implementation detail: normalize structured outputs before schema_accuracy: lowercase, remove punctuation except decimal separators, collapse whitespace, map synonyms (yes/yeah/affirm).

ci-bot: eval-harness/ci/model-onboard/1765010000 queued model=redwood-qlm-7b quant=4bit SUITE=canary-40

ci-bot: run finished. results -> schema_accuracy:0.905 (baseline 0.937, p=0.009 after BH), norm_levenshtein:0.071 (baseline 0.048, p=0.02), embed_cosine_mean:0.820 (baseline 0.835, p=0.11), token_coverage:0.975 (baseline 0.991, p=0.06). worst_intent_drop: 0.034 for "payment.setup". verdict: HOLD_CANARY

Eve Tran: Not greatschema_accuracy and norm_levenshtein failed the threshold/p test and payment.setup exceeded 3pp. We should block canary rollouts until triage.

Marta Ruiz: Auto-create ticket with artifacts (sanitized prompts, baseline vs candidate outputs, token diffs, per-intent breakdown). If quant is suspected, run an 8bit and FP16 ablation.

Diego Morales: Also log the exact failing prompts to s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/1765010000/failed-prompts.txt (sanitized). Add a quick decoder-arg check to the artifact bundle so we can see sampling/temperature differences.

Hannah Li: Action plan: 1) CI marks model HOLD_CANARY, 2) system creates RED-ML-4007 with triage checklist, 3) run quant ablations + full regression suite, 4) human triage within 36h.

ci-bot: created ticket RED-ML-4007: "HOLD_CANARY redwood-qlm-7b 4bit payment.setup regression" artifacts: https://ci.redwood/test-runs/1765010000

Eve Tran: I'll update the onboarding checklist to require canary-40 pass for any canary, include the JSON policy fields (suite, metrics, stats, actions), auto-block on HOLD_CANARY, and require prompts to be curated into a canary set repo.

Diego Morales: One more ask: include a fast pre-flight heuristic in CI that checks only schema_accuracy on a 10-example smoke if you want super-fast gating before the full canary run.

Marta Ruiz: Good idea. Add that as an optional preflight mode: PRE_FLIGHT_10 with relaxed thresholds and only schema_accuracy + token_coverage. If PRE_FLIGHT_10 fails, abort earlier.

Eve Tran: Thanks all. I'll open the PR for the harness schema, canary-40 set, and the CI job. Ping me if you want to help curate the payment.setup adversarial variants. :sparkles:
